problemSigns.detail: Rollers make noise as the garage door moves up or down. This indicates worn bearings or flat spots on the roller wheel.
The garage door shakes or moves unevenly in the track. This often means rollers are not rolling smoothly.
Inspect the rollers directly. You might see flattened areas on the wheel or a noticeable wobble during operation.
The metal shaft connecting the roller to the hinge can rust or bend. This impedes proper movement and can cause binding.

faqs.q: What kind of rollers are best for Arlington Heights homes, especially older ones?
faqs.a: For homes in areas like Pioneer Park or Berkley Square, built in the 1950s and 60s, sealed-bearing nylon rollers are often a good choice. They run quietly and do not require lubrication, which helps with noise under bedrooms. Newer homes, such as those around Lake Arlington from the 1990s, also benefit from these quiet options. Steel rollers offer maximum durability in heavier doors.

faqs.q: Why do garage door rollers wear out so quickly in the Chicago area?
faqs.a: Chicago-area weather significantly impacts roller lifespan. The extreme temperature swings from summer humidity to harsh winters cause materials to expand and contract. This stresses roller bearings and plastic wheels. Rust is common on steel roller stems due to moisture. Older homes in Downtown Arlington or Scarsdale may have original rollers that are simply past their functional life. Regular use also contributes to wear.

faqs.q: Do you perform a safety check after roller replacement?
faqs.a: Yes, after every garage door service, including roller replacement, we conduct a full balance and safety-reverse test. This ensures the door operates correctly and safely. It also verifies that your opener is not overstressed. This step is standard for all our repairs in Arlington Heights and throughout Chicagoland.
